subject: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Fisher <emma.fisher@novacare.com>, legal@novacare.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request

Hi Emma / NovaCare legal,

Thanks again for the productive commercial call yesterday. As we move toward signing the order form, procurement has pushed back on our standard confidentiality carve-out: they want a clear path to recover in the event of trade-secret misappropriation.

To avoid a deadlock, we're proposing the following narrow carve-out to the liability cap in the MSA (attached as "proposed_msa_clause.txt") for your legal review:

- Exclude from the liability cap any damages arising from willful misappropriation or unauthorized disclosure of Customer trade secrets by Redwood or its agents.
- Preserve rights to equitable relief (injunctions) and recovery of forensic costs and reasonable attorneys' fees incurred to investigate and remediate a confirmed exfiltration.
- Trigger: customer provides a validated forensic report demonstrating unauthorized access or extraction of trade-secret material.

I've attached a redlined order form (redline_orderform_v2.docx) that highlights where we'd like the carve-out to live. This is intentionally narrow — the goal is to make sure material trade-secret events aren't swallowed by a general fee cap.

Can your team review and flag any non-starters? If you prefer, we can provide a short mutual action plan and vendor list for forensic work.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Strategic Account Manager | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redline_orderform_v2.docx (redline), proposed_msa_clause.txt (plain text proposal)

From: Emma Fisher <emma.fisher@novacare.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@novacare.com, procurement@novacare.com
Date: Sun, 8 Apr 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the context and the narrow ask. I circulated this to our legal and procurement teams. A few initial points:

1) We are sympathetic to protecting trade secrets, but "unlimited damages" language is a non-starter for our GC team without objective thresholds.
2) We need a clearer incident definition (what constitutes "trade-secret exfiltration") and evidence requirements (forensic vendor, scope, timeline).
3) Procurement asks that any recoverable forensic fees have a pre-approved cap unless the disclosure obviously meets a high wilfulness standard.

I'll loop in our legal counsel (legal@novacare.com) and procurement to start drafting counter-language. Happy to schedule a 30-min sync early next week.

Emma Fisher
Head of Strategic Procurement | NovaCare Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: legal@novacare.com, Emma Fisher <emma.fisher@novacare.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request

Emma — thanks for the quick reply and for surfacing procurement's cap concerns.

We want to propose a bridging text that preserves your need for predictability while ensuring material trade-secret theft isn't effectively immunized by the general fee cap. High-level proposal (attached as a clean redline: MSA_redline_trade_secret_exclusion_20280409.pdf):

- "The liability cap shall not apply to damages arising fromwillful misappropriation of Customer trade secrets where such misappropriation is demonstrated by a validated forensic analysis concluding unauthorized extraction of designated trade-secret materials.
- Forensic costs and reasonable remediation expenses incurred by Customer will be recoverable; Redwood will not contest reasonableness if the investigation is performed by a mutually agreed vendor or one from Redwood's approved forensics list.
- As a safety valve, where forensic costs exceed $100,000, recovery of excess costs shall be subject to mediator-led review (fees split equally) unless there is a final judicial or arbitral finding of willful conduct.
- Trigger mechanics: preservation notice within 7 days, preservation of logs and snapshots, and delivery of forensic report within 30 days of engagement.

This aims to: (a) create an objective trigger, (b) cap unexpected forensic spend in typical cases, and (c) keep unlimited recovery available only where willfulness is shown by a final adjudication.

Quoted for context: "We need a clearer incident definition (what constitutes 'trade-secret exfiltration') and evidence requirements (forensic vendor, scope, timeline)." — Emma

If that framework is acceptable in principle, let's convert it into a short mutual action plan and an updated order form redline.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: NovaCare Legal <legal@novacare.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request

Laura / Tessa — thanks for the suggested bridge language. A few points from our side after internal review:

- We cannot accept an open-ended "unlimited" recovery right triggered by a vendor report alone. We need the recovery to be either (1) capped at a multiple of paid fees (we propose 3x net fees in the prior 12 months) or (2) unlimited only after a final judicial or arbitral determination of willfulness.
- If Redwood insists on immediate recovery of forensic costs, we require a pre-approved vendor list and a per-incident cap on vendor costs (we propose $75,000) to avoid surprise invoices.
- We will accept preservation timelines, but request that Redwood reimburse only reasonable forensic costs where the report validates actual data loss to a third party — internal access incidents not leading to leakage should not automatically trigger full recovery.

Please see inline comments on your redline (we returned a version via procurement portal). Procurement is prepared to proceed quickly if we can land on a compromise for forensic-cost caps and the condition precedent for unlimited recovery.

--
NovaCare Legal
legal@novacare.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Fisher <emma.fisher@novacare.com>, legal@novacare.com
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, finance@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2028 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order form negotiation — confidentiality / trade-secret carve-out request

Emma / NovaCare legal — thanks for the candid feedback and for returning redlines. We want to close this matter without slowing the wider deal (DEAL-4729). Proposed compromise below for your review:

1) Liability cap carve-out: Unlimited recovery will be available only for willful misappropriation of Customer-designated trade secrets, and only where willfulness is determined by either: (a) final judgment in court, or (b) binding arbitration ruling.

2) Interim remedies & forensic costs: Customer may recover reasonable forensic costs and provisional remediation expenses upon delivery of a validated forensic report from a mutually agreed vendor. Reimbursement of forensic costs exceeding $100,000 per incident will be subject to either (i) Redwood pre-approval for the vendor engagement, or (ii) mediator review within 30 days (costs of mediator split 50/50).

3) Third-party leakage threshold: Unlimited recovery is limited to incidents where the validated forensic report demonstrates unauthorized transfer of trade-secret material to an external third party or publication to a public forum. Internal-only access (no leakage) will be limited to fee-based recovery up to 3x prior 12-month fees.

4) Vendor list & caps: We attach Redwood's approved forensics vendor list (vendor-forensics-approved-list.csv). If Customer insists on a specific vendor outside the list, parties will agree budget caps in advance; absent agreement, Redwood's caps apply.

5) Mutual action plan: We prepared a short MAP (mutual_action_plan_DEAL-4729.xlsx) with clear owner assignments and SLOs for investigation and remediation. We request procurement sign-off on the MAP before we exchange final SIGNATURE copies of the order form.

Next steps:
- Please confirm whether NovaCare will accept the binding-adjudication trigger for unlimited recovery OR whether you require unlimited recovery be available upon vendor report alone (we anticipate your answer will drive whether this closes or needs GC escalation).
- If acceptable, procurement, legal, and finance can finalize numeric caps in the MAP and we can sign the order form by EOD Friday.

If helpful, I can hop on a 30-min call with your GC and procurement tomorrow.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
